notMeasured.reason: A write measured with COMMIT mutates the corpus and makes the run non-repeatable; measured with ROLLBACK it omits the WAL flush, which is the dominant cost. Neither is worth a baseline.
As Task create, plus optimistic-concurrency retry cost that does not exist until the command layer does.
A transition is a command with guard evaluation, dependency checks, and four writes in one transaction (docs/23). Its SQL alone would understate it by more than it measures.
There is no cache. The docs/30 target is a property of the epoch-keyed cache in docs/04, which is Phase 1 code.
No API process exists. Every number here is a database round trip and excludes everything the server does around it.
Cases run single-threaded, one query in flight. Contention, pool saturation, and the read/write mix in docs/30 §Throughput are not exercised.

baseline.justification: First reference-tooling baseline for the m4-10c-16gb environment (F-007). Corpus is tools/casual-task-seed --scale small (50,000 tasks), generated after the one-level comment-threading fix, loaded into a clean PostgreSQL 16 and ANALYZEd. Recorded on an otherwise idle machine. NOT a gating baseline: docs/30 names an 8 vCPU / 32 GB reference machine and this is a laptop, so the harness will refuse to compare a run from anywhere else against it. It exists as the worked example benchmarks/README.md points new work at, replacing smoke-local.smoke.json's hand-written corpus with the real generator, and as a real datapoint for the docs/30 targets at a scale that fits a developer machine. Every case is far inside its docs/30 p95 target at this scale; full_text_search at 17.1 ms is the one to watch, because D-043 shows its plan degrades to a sequential scan under RLS at reference scale.
